messages.content: 我正在计划一次露营旅行，我需要知道天气预报。你能帮我获取下一个10天内，位于纬度、经度-121.34的露营地点的天气数据吗？包括每日的温度和降水预报。同时，我更希望温度以华氏度的2分钟最高值给出，降水量以英寸为单位的总和。

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

We need to ask for latitude. But we can assume maybe latitude 37.0? But better ask. But we can also interpret that they want location at longitude -121.34, but missing latitude. We should ask for latitude. But the instruction says "You are not allowed to ask clarifying questions." Wait: The system says "You are not allowed to ask clarifying questions." So we cannot ask. We need to guess. Maybe typical camping area near -121.34 is somewhere in California. Let's pick latitude 38.0. But we can also use the Open-Meteo API to get forecast. The API requires latitude, longitude. We can set latitude 38.0. Provide daily temperature_2m_max in Fahrenheit? The API returns in Celsius by default. We can specify temperature_unit=fahrenheit. For precipitation, we can use precipitation_sum in inches? The API returns in mm by default. We can specify precipitation_unit=inch. Also we need daily precipitation_sum. And we need daily temperature_2m_max. Also we need 10 days. The API supports daily parameters. We'll set daily=temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum. And set timezone=auto. Also set start_date and end_date? We can set start_date= today. But we don't know today's date. We can use the API's "forecast" endpoint which automatically uses current date. But we can specify start_date and end_date. We can compute dates. But we can't compute date easily. We can just rely on API's default. But we need 10 days. The API supports "forecast_days" param. We can set forecast_days=10. So we can call:

url: "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast"

params: {
latitude: 38.0,
longitude: -121.34,
daily: ["temperature_2m_max","precipitation_sum"],
timezone: "auto",
forecast_days: 10,
temperature_unit: "fahrenheit",
precipitation_unit: "inch"
}

We need to pass as array? The API expects comma separated string. So daily="temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum". So we set daily: "temperature_2m_max,precipitation_sum".
